biology.cloning-recall-multi.0004.a: e.g. antithrombin / alpha-1-antitrypsin / clotting factor in milk

biology.comprehension-altitude.0001.a: Fewer oxygen molecules per breath; so breathe faster to take in enough oxygen for respiration
biology.comprehension-altitude.0001.b: Biconcave/large SA for diffusion; no nucleus so more haemoglobin; haemoglobin binds oxygen
biology.comprehension-altitude.0001.e: Mutation produced allele / variation; those with allele survived better in low oxygen; reproduced and passed allele on; frequency increased over generations
biology.comprehension-altitude.0001.f: Not enough oxygen supplied to muscles; anaerobic respiration; glucose to lactic acid
biology.comprehension-altitude.0001.g: More haemoglobin so more oxygen carried to muscles; more aerobic respiration / more energy, less lactic acid
biology.comprehension-altitude.0001.h: Thicker blood more likely to clot / flows slowly; clot blocks coronary artery so heart muscle starved of oxygen

biology.comprehension-bees.0001.b: Large brightly coloured petals; strong scent; nectar (nectaries) as food reward
biology.comprehension-bees.0001.c: Dissolved in water absorbed by roots; transported in xylem in transpiration stream to all parts
biology.comprehension-bees.0001.d: Neurotransmitter released from end of neurone, diffuses across gap, binds to receptors on next neurone triggering impulse
biology.comprehension-bees.0001.f: Any two: same number of colonies (25), same food (pollen and sugar solution), same time of exposure (6 weeks), same field, same concentration
biology.comprehension-bees.0001.g: Fewer flowers pollinated; fewer fertilised; fewer fruits/seeds; lower yield
biology.comprehension-bees.0001.h: Specific to pest so does not harm bees/other organisms; no chemical residues/bioaccumulation; no resistance; long-lasting

biology.comprehension-cassava.0001.b: Phloem carries sucrose/amino acids (translocation); source of food/energy for whitefly
biology.comprehension-cassava.0001.c: Cuttings produced by asexual reproduction / mitosis; virus present in all tissues/sap of parent so passed on
biology.comprehension-cassava.0001.g: Cross resistant variety with high-yield variety; select offspring with both resistance and high yield; breed these; repeat over many generations
biology.comprehension-cassava.0001.h: Adv: resistant, higher yield (22.5 vs 9), reduces famine; Disadv: genes may spread to wild relatives, effects on insects, cost/seed

biology.comprehension-coral.0001.b: Tentacles/mouth catch small animals (feed on other organisms); soft body; produce nitrogenous waste; cannot photosynthesise
biology.comprehension-coral.0001.c: Algae photosynthesise giving coral glucose and amino acids; coral provides CO2 for photosynthesis and nitrogen waste for amino acid/protein synthesis; algae get shelter
biology.comprehension-coral.0001.e: Burning fossil fuels / deforestation release CO2 (and methane from cattle); enhanced greenhouse effect; more heat/infrared trapped; global warming raises sea temperature
biology.comprehension-coral.0001.g: Coral died so less food/shelter; fish starve or move away / eaten by predators
biology.comprehension-coral.0001.h: Sewage adds nutrients causing algal growth blocking light; bacteria decompose and respire using oxygen; less oxygen/light for coral and algae; pathogens

biology.comprehension-dengue.0001.d: Bacterium lives in cytoplasm of eggs; every egg receives cytoplasm from mother so all offspring infected
biology.comprehension-dengue.0001.f: Antibodies produced by lymphocytes only in response to dengue antigens; specific so presence shows infection
biology.comprehension-dengue.0001.g: Other half acts as control for comparison; to show reduction caused by Wolbachia not other factors
biology.comprehension-dengue.0001.h: Random mutation gives resistance; resistant mosquitoes survive spraying; reproduce passing on allele; resistance becomes common
biology.comprehension-dengue.0001.i: Fish/dragonfly larvae/birds/bats lose food source so their populations fall; may eat other prey instead

biology.comprehension-diabetes.0001.b: Insulin causes liver and muscle cells to take up glucose; liver converts glucose to glycogen to store; blood glucose falls
biology.comprehension-diabetes.0001.d: Working muscles respire more, using more glucose; take up glucose from blood even without insulin
biology.comprehension-diabetes.0001.e: More aerobic respiration; more energy (ATP) released for contraction; less lactic acid
biology.comprehension-diabetes.0001.f: Large sample (3000); long period (3 years); control group given no advice
biology.comprehension-diabetes.0001.h: Too much glucose filtered; cannot all be reabsorbed (carriers saturated) so some remains in urine
biology.comprehension-diabetes.0001.i: Inherit alleles that increase risk; families share similar diet/lifestyle

biology.comprehension-lactose.0001.b: 37 near optimum - frequent collisions/substrate fits active site; at 60 denatured - active site shape changed so substrate cannot bind
biology.comprehension-lactose.0001.c: Ll x Ll -> LL, Ll, Ll, ll; ll non-persistent; probability 1/4 (0.25, 25%)
biology.comprehension-lactose.0001.e: Mutation produced L allele; people with L could digest milk, more likely to survive food shortage and reproduce; pass on L; frequency increases over generations
biology.comprehension-lactose.0001.f: Bacteria convert lactose to lactic acid so less lactose; less lactose reaches large intestine for gas-producing bacteria
biology.comprehension-lactose.0001.g: Lactase breaks down lactose to glucose and galactose; glucose absorbed into blood in small intestine
biology.comprehension-lactose.0001.h: Undigested lactose reaches large intestine; bacteria respire anaerobically on it producing gases (CO2)
biology.comprehension-lactose.0001.i: Healthy bones/teeth; blood clotting; muscle contraction

biology.comprehension-seagrass.0001.c: Little oxygen; decomposers (bacteria/fungi) cannot respire aerobically so decomposition slow
biology.comprehension-seagrass.0001.e: Nitrates cause algal growth/bloom blocking light; seagrass cannot photosynthesise and dies; (decomposers use up oxygen)
biology.comprehension-seagrass.0001.g: Place frames at random; count shoots in each of many frames; calculate mean per 0.25 m2; multiply to per m2 (x4) then by 360 000 m2
biology.comprehension-seagrass.0001.h: Seagrass absorbs CO2 in photosynthesis and stores carbon in roots/mud; less CO2 in atmosphere reduces greenhouse effect

biology.comprehension-sickle.0001.b: Each amino acid coded by triplet of bases (codon); change in one base changes the codon so a different amino acid
biology.comprehension-sickle.0001.c: Sickle cells destroyed quickly / carry less oxygen; less oxygen to cells; less aerobic respiration so less energy
biology.comprehension-sickle.0001.e: AS x AS -> AA, AS, AS, SS; SS has disease; probability 1/4
biology.comprehension-sickle.0001.f: Carriers less likely to die from malaria; survive and reproduce; pass on S allele; so allele frequency high (natural selection)
biology.comprehension-sickle.0001.g: Donor marrow stem cells have normal alleles; divide and differentiate into red blood cells with normal haemoglobin
biology.comprehension-sickle.0001.h: Adv: early treatment/care; Disadv: stress/anxiety, cost, small risk/consent issues

biology.comprehension-soil-antibiotic.00.b: Reduces competition for nutrients/space; so more resources for them to grow and reproduce
biology.comprehension-soil-antibiotic.00.c: Diffusion through the partially permeable membrane; from high concentration in soil to low in holes; membrane lets small molecules through but not bacteria
biology.comprehension-soil-antibiotic.00.e: Control; to show that survival was due to the antibiotic, not the injection itself
biology.comprehension-soil-antibiotic.00.f: human cells do not have a cell wall
biology.comprehension-soil-antibiotic.00.g: Mutation gives resistance; antibiotic kills non-resistant bacteria; resistant ones survive and reproduce; overuse of antibiotics in hospitals; spread between patients
biology.comprehension-soil-antibiotic.00.h: Target is not a protein so not coded directly by a gene; one mutation changes one protein only
biology.comprehension-soil-antibiotic.00.i: May be toxic to humans/side effects; check safe dose; may work differently in humans

biology.comprehension-tb.0001.b: Phagocytes engulf bacteria (phagocytosis); digest them with enzymes
biology.comprehension-tb.0001.c: Reduced surface area for gas exchange; less oxygen diffuses into blood; scar tissue thickens - longer diffusion distance; so breathe faster
biology.comprehension-tb.0001.e: Contains antigens similar to TB; lymphocytes produce antibodies and memory cells; on infection memory cells produce antibodies rapidly in large numbers
biology.comprehension-tb.0001.f: Not all bacteria killed; resistant ones survive; reproduce; resistant strain spreads
biology.comprehension-tb.0001.g: Double blind to avoid bias; placebo effect; doctors' judgement not influenced

biology.comprehension-vertical-farm.0001.a: Farms built close to the shops so vegetables travel only a few km
biology.comprehension-vertical-farm.0001.b: Nitrate for amino acids/proteins; magnesium for chlorophyll
biology.comprehension-vertical-farm.0001.c: Supply oxygen to roots for aerobic respiration; energy for active transport of mineral ions
biology.comprehension-vertical-farm.0001.d: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light; used for photosynthesis; green reflected so wasted
biology.comprehension-vertical-farm.0001.e: CO2 is a reactant/limiting factor so more photosynthesis; 24 C near optimum for enzymes; more glucose for growth
biology.comprehension-vertical-farm.0001.h: No chemical residues/specific to pest/does not harm other organisms; no resistance
biology.comprehension-vertical-farm.0001.i: Better: less water, no pesticides, less transport fuel, less land; Worse: electricity from fossil fuels contributes to climate change

biology.crops-data-graph.0004.a: Yield increases as fertiliser increases then levels off at high fertiliser; quote data
biology.crops-data-graph.0004.b: Fertiliser provides nitrate; used to make amino acids/proteins for growth; more growth/photosynthesis so higher yield; levels off as another factor limits

biology.crops-data-pct.0001.b: Yield increases as CO2 increases because CO2 is limiting factor for photosynthesis; levels off at high CO2 because another factor (light/temperature) limits

biology.crops-data-plot.0004.a: Axes correct with labels/units; linear scale; points plotted; smooth curve
biology.crops-data-plot.0004.b: Yield increases with fertiliser up to 200 kg/ha then levels off at 5.6 t/ha; increase becomes smaller

biology.crops-data-read.0002.c: CO2 limiting so photosynthesis rises; then levels off as another factor limits

biology.crops-describe-multi.0003.b: Add fertiliser containing nitrates/phosphate/potassium; nitrate used to make proteins for growth; add correct amount at right time

biology.crops-explain.0006.all: Pesticides may kill non-target organisms e.g. pollinators; bioaccumulation along food chain; toxic concentration in top predators

biology.crops-explain-multi.0002.b: Kill non-target species; accumulate in food chains; reach toxic levels in top consumers

biology.crops-mcq-rev.0008.all: Supplies mineral ions such as nitrate to the soil
